correctness.rationale: For each of the k accepted words choose a length-two accepting path. Two chosen paths cannot share the middle state, since splicing them would accept an off-diagonal word. A middle state cannot be initial or final, since then a word of length one is accepted. Three such middle states with the same final force two distinct four-cycles sharing an edge at the initial state. Thus at least ceil(k/2) distinct finals are needed. Pairing the paths at their finals realizes this bound with four-cycles meeting only at the start and a pendant path for an odd singleton. A shared final attains the unrestricted bound k+2, including k=1,2 where the overhead is zero. The proof counts states, not transitions, and covers nonunambiguous NFAs.
residual_risks: The finite enumeration is corroboration only; the general lower bound and construction give the result.
